definition: In semantics and text extraction, name resolution refers to the ability of text mining software to determine which actual person, actor, or object a particular use of a name refers to.
details: It can also be referred to as entity resolution.

explainer.lead: Name resolution is the ability of text mining software to determine which actual person, actor or object a particular use of a name refers to. It is also called entity resolution.

tiers.eli5: It's how software works out that two mentions of a name in different documents are talking about the same real person or thing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to merge mentions scattered across text into single identities; a pitfall is ambiguity when different entities share a name or one entity appears under several names.
tiers.paperLevel: It determines the actual referent of a name use, resolving ambiguity across mentions; accuracy is limited by name variation and shared names.

explainer.example: The mentions 'J. Smith' and 'John Smith' in two articles are resolved to the same individual.
